verses.text: Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be moved; it abides forever.
As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people, both now and forevermore.
For the scepter of the wicked will not rest upon the land allotted to the righteous, so that the righteous will not put forth their hands to injustice.
Do good, O LORD, to those who are good, and to the upright in heart.
But those who turn to crooked ways the LORD will banish with the evildoers. Peace be upon Israel.

context.author: The title calls it “A song of ascents,” one of fifteen such psalms (120-134). They may have been sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts; the Mishnah says the Levites sang them on the fifteen steps inside the Temple courts (Sukkah 5:4).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: “Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be moved; it abides forever. As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people, both now and forevermore” (vv.1-2). Foreign rule will not last: “the scepter of the wicked will not rest upon the land allotted to the righteous,” so that the righteous are not tempted to do wrong (v.3). “Do good, O LORD, to those who are good, and to the upright in heart” (v.4), but the crooked will be banished with evildoers. “Peace be upon Israel” (v.5).
context.custom: Jerusalem is ringed by higher hills: the Mount of Olives to the east, Mount Scopus to the north-east, and ridges to the south and west. A pilgrim arriving would see the city sheltered by them. The scepter of the wicked (v.3) may mean foreign rulers over the land, as under Persia after the exile.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 126, the next Song of Ascents, remembers when the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion.
context.timelineBible: Jesus said the one who hears and does His words is like a man who built his house on the rock, which did not fall (Matthew 7:24-25). Paul ends Galatians, “Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God” (Galatians 6:16), like v.5.

overview.summary: Those who trust in the LORD are as unshakable as Mount Zion, and as the mountains surround Jerusalem, the LORD surrounds His people; the rule of the wicked will not last, and peace will be on Israel.
overview.settingLine: A city ringed by hills, a people ringed by God.

history.t: The scepter of the wicked over the land.

archaeology.t: An ancient Jewish cemetery covers its slopes facing the Temple Mount.
The Kidron and Hinnom valleys and the hills around them.

overview.discussion: “As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people” (v.2). Where do I need to remember that God is all around me?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-125 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Not named
